events.title: Win Streak May End For Malaysia Stock Market
events.description: The Malaysia stock market has finished higher in four straight sessions, collecting almost 30 points or 1.8 percent along the way. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now sits just shy of the 1,630-point plateau although the rally may stall on Thursday.

events.title: Japan Stock Market May Extend Losing Streak On Thursday
events.description: The Japan stock market has tracked lower in five straight sessions, slumping more than 2,930 points or 4.2 percent in that span. The Nikkei now sits just beneath the 67,750-point plateau and it's looking at another soft start again on Thursday.

events.title: Dramatically Oversold KOSPI Still Called Lower On Thursday
events.description: The South Korea stock market has finished lower in six straight sessions, plummeting more than 1,000 points or 15 percent along the way. The KOSPI now sits just above the 6,000-point plateau and it's got another weak lead for Thursday's trade.

events.title: Australia Unemployment Data Due On Thursday
events.description: Australia will on Thursday release September data for unemployment, highlighting a modest day for Asia-Pacific economic activity. The jobless rate is expected to hold steady at 4.6 percent, with the addition of 20.0K jobs following the addition of 39.5K in August.

events.title: Swiss Market Closes On Strong Note
events.description: After a flat start, Swiss stocks kept edging higher and higher on Wednesday thanks to sustained buying at several counters and eventually ended the session on a buoyant note, extending gains to a fourth straight session.

events.title: Major European Markets Close On Firm Note
events.description: The major European markets closed on the positive side on Wednesday even as several markets in the region failed to hold early gains. The early buoyancy over upbeat earnings update from Dutch semiconductor equipment maker ASML subsided a bit later on in the session.

events.title: U.S. Core Consumer Prices Rise More Than Expected In September
events.description: While the Labor Department released a report on Wednesday showing consumer prices in the U.S. grew in line with estimates in the month of September, the report also showed a bigger than expected increase in core consumer prices, which exclude food and energy prices. The report said consumer prices climbed by 0.6 percent in September after rising by 0.4 percent in August.

events.title: Bay Street Likely To Open With Slightly Positive Bias
events.description: Canadian stocks may open with a positive bias on Wednesday, but the upside is likely to be limited amid a mixed trend in commodities markets. U.S. inflation data is likely to make an impact.

events.title: Bank Of America Q3 Profit Drops On $1.2 Bln Treasury Fine; Shares Hit
events.description: Shares of Bank of America Corp. were losing around 6 percent in the pre-market activity on the NYSE after the banking major reported lower third-quarter earnings, hurt by a $1.2 billion fine imposed by the U.S. Department of the Treasury on anti-money laundering issues. Revenues, however, increased with higher net interest income and growth in consumer Banking as well as Global Wealth and Invest

events.title: U.S. Consumer Prices Increase In Line With Estimates In September
events.description: Partly reflecting a spike in energy prices, the Labor Department released a closely watched report on Wednesday showing consumer prices in the U.S. increased in line with economist estimates in the month of September.

events.title: Pound Rises As UK Chancellor Assures Fiscal Discipline
events.description: The British pound strengthened against other major currencies in the European session on Wednesday, as UK Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey promises to finance the cost-of-living support package through increased taxes or cuts in public spending rather than further borrowing.

events.title: China Inflation Rises Marginally; PPI Inflation Strongest Since 2022
events.description: China's consumer price inflation rose only slightly in September due to the fall in food prices, and remained sluggish when compared to global peers, while producer price inflation reached its highest level in over four years on rising commodity prices. Consumer prices rose 0.9 percent in September from a year ago, slightly faster than the 0.8 percent increase seen in August.

events.title: FTSE 100 Modestly Higher In Cautious Trade
events.description: The UK stock market's FTSE 100 moved modestly higher on Wednesday with stocks turning in a mixed performance amid a lack of fresh earnings or economic data from the home front. The mood remained slightly cautious as investors looked ahead to the U.S. crucial consumer price inflation data later in the day.
